subject: POC hosting matrix, runway & clear next steps
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@mednova.com>, Samir Patel <samir@mednova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: POC hosting matrix, runway & clear next steps

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap of what we agreed and a proposed, pragmatic hosting matrix so we can lock the runway for the POC: what success looks like, what we’ll measure, and who owns each piece. I’ve attached a short matrix (poc_runway_matrix.xlsx) and our trial terms (redwood_trial_terms_v2.pdf).

High-level recap (agreed on call):
- Success criteria (we need these validated by your team):
  - End-to-end latency for API calls under 300ms p50 for interactive flows (50k Token/session cap)
  - 99.5% availability for the trial window; tolerable fallbacks but must not drop customer-facing features
  - Model output fidelity on our canonical prompt set: >90% pass rate on the pilot eval (we will run an eval harness)
  - Data handling: logs retained for 30 days, telemetry available to your SREs (read-only)

Hosting matrix (summary):
1) Hosted (Redwood API): fastest onboarding — recommended if you want to move quickly and validate UX.
  - Time to test: <48 hours.
  - Pros: no infra ops, rapid iteration, lowest short-term friction.
  - Cons: token-level audit visibility limited to dashboard exports; not suitable if you need customer-provisioned networking.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity in Redwood-managed pool): medium setup time — good balance for predictable latency and cost.
  - Time to test: 3–7 business days (provisioning + data gating).
  - Pros: guaranteed throughput, model pinning, per-customer telemetry.
  - Cons: requires commit for the reserved pool window, somewhat longer procurement cycle.
3) VPC Private (VPC Peering / On-prem connector): longest setup but required for regulated data or strict network controls.
  - Time to test: 2–4 weeks (network setup, security review, KMS integration).
  - Pros: full network isolation, customer-managed KMS options, audit logs directed to your SIEM.
  - Cons: longer lead time and additional operational ownership on your side.

Recommended path for MedNova (proposal):
- Start on Hosted for a two-week technical validation (rapid UX/quality checks + eval harness). Parallel work: procurement & security paperwork for Dedicated.
- If performance/visibility requirements are confirmed (you hit thresholds in the matrix), move to Dedicated sandbox for the bulk of the POC (4–6 weeks).
- VPC only if internal compliance mandates it for production; we can scope that in parallel.

Immediate asks / next steps: (action owners in parens)
- Elena / Samir: Confirm the success criteria above or send edits by EOD Mon (11/23) so we can finalize the evaluation prompts and load targets (MedNova).
- Procurement: review redwood_trial_terms_v2.pdf and flag any redlines; preferred: two-week hosted validation + 6-week dedicated sandbox (Procurement).
- OLGA: I’ll schedule environment provisioning tasks once we have sign-off; I’ll also spin up the eval harness and share access to the benchmark dashboard.
- BEN: Please hold a provisional Dedicated pool slot for MedNova week-of Dec 6–Dec 12 (Ben).

Attachments: poc_runway_matrix.xlsx (summary matrix), redwood_trial_terms_v2.pdf

Thanks —
Olga

--
Olga Petrov

Thanks, Olga — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: 300ms p50 is OK for most flows; one exception — document ingestion/semantic search must be <500ms p95 for 10k-doc index in your hosted test environment. Can you include that in the eval harness?
- Audit logs: we need a nightly export to our S3 bucket (read-only) during the Dedicated window; is that available?
- Security: our InfoSec will need the SOC2 attestation and an initial answers packet; I’ve looped procurement to start formal review.

Assuming those points are feasible, we’re fine to start with the Hosted quick validation for two weeks, then move to Dedicated. Also — pricing question: if we move to Dedicated for 6 weeks, what’s the expected committed minimum and will there be a pilot discount?

Elena
Director of Product, MedNova Health
elena@mednova.com
